results.reason: Issue 1 identifies that §9.4(c) removes the 10% cap and the basket for all §9.2(a) claims, which cover any representation and not only Fundamental Representations. It explains that exposure is uncapped and well beyond the escrow. It recommends narrowing the carve-out to Fundamental Representations and fraud.

Issue 3 identifies that TSA §9.3 selects Delaware law and courts, conflicting with New York in the other documents. It explains that §10.12 lets the TSA control its own subject matter, so the conflict is not cured. It notes the risk of split and parallel proceedings and recommends conforming the TSA to New York law and forum.

Issue 2 identifies that Bill of Sale §1.1(b) has no Excluded Assets carve-out and no cross-reference to the APA. It explains that the Bill of Sale could convey the cash, the Albany facility and the HOLLIS mark, and that §10.12 does not rescue Seller. It recommends adopting the APA definition with an express exclusion.
The memo states the cap is 10% of the Purchase Price, which is $1,840,000 on an $18,400,000 price, and equals the Escrow Amount.
The memo lists Seller's cash, the Albany manufacturing facility and the HOLLIS trademark as Excluded Assets under APA §2.2.
Each issue sets out the document and section, why it matters to Marrowind, and a recommended fix, in a memo format.
The issues are expressly ordered by significance, with the most significant first. Part IV is a separate section for items requiring a client business decision.
The memo expressly states that §10.12 does not cure Issues 2 or 3.
The memo expressly states that neither the 10% cap nor the escrow limits Seller's liability for ordinary representation breaches.
